bugs.error_message: IndexError: list index out of range when writing patched TMX
bugs.root_cause: ET.tostring(root, encoding='UTF-8') was assumed to emit an XML declaration that could be split off with .split(b'?>\n',1)[1]; it did not emit one in that form, so index [1] was out of range.
bugs.fix: Use ET.tostring(root, encoding='utf-8', xml_declaration=False) and prepend the desired b'<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n' literal. Note ET emits single-quoted declarations, which is why the literal is needed to byte-match the original files.

bugs.error_message: [gold priors] eflomal.calculate_priors failed for en: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str
bugs.root_cause: A gold record (sentence_id 0, 'lefe texto' <-> 'Preface') carries links [[0,1],[1,2],[0,0],[1,0]] while the stored target has only 1 token, so j=1 and j=2 are out of bounds. eflomal.calculate_priors raises on the first out-of-bounds link, and its own error path is buggy -- `raise ValueError('Invalid input on line %d' % lineno + 1)` evaluates as (str % int) + int, so a TypeError masks the real 'alignment out of bounds' message. Because the bad record was first in the list, ALL 54 gold records were silently discarded (run_giza_improved catches the exception and prints '[gold priors] skipped').
bugs.fix: _pharaoh() now takes optional n_src/n_tgt and drops links pointing past either token list, returning (pharaoh_string, dropped_count). append_gold_priors() passes the token counts, logs which sentence_id had out-of-bounds links, and warns that those rows are stale and need re-annotation. Verified: all 54 gold records now yield 364 LEX / 13 HMMF / 14 HMMR / 261 FERF / 271 FERR priors.

bugs.error_message: apkg_image_sync.py read Anki image fields by hardcoded ordinal (img=14, src=15, gif=19, gif_src=20); ordinal 14 is IntransitiveCu in the current notetype
bugs.root_cause: IMAGE_NOTETYPES hardcoded field positions captured before AnkiMaker3 v3 inserted the per-VerbType fields (Transitive..State, ords 11-18). That pushed the image fields from 14/15/19/20 to 19/20/24/25, so the sync silently read verb-type text as image URLs. The second notetype's offsets (Globasa lexi SabziFruta) were wrong too.
bugs.fix: Resolve field ordinals from the apkg's own `fields` table by NAME (Imajelinku, ImajeAsel, DuayumImaje, DuayumImajeAsel, Faleanimalinku, Faleanimaasel). Same rule as word-list.csv: use header names, never positions. Verified against the live deck: ntid 1761931224511 -> 19/20/22/23/24/25, ntid 1762076920706 -> 8/9/11/12.

bugs.error_message: apkg_image_sync re-imported 4 images the store already had, under their pre-rename titles
bugs.root_cause: resolve_commons_images.py adopts the canonical title when the MediaWiki API follows a file redirect, but discarded the old one. The Anki deck still holds the pre-rename URL, so the identity check saw a different file and adopted the same picture twice (e.g. Europe-Bosnia_and_Herzegovina.svg vs Map_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_in_Europe.svg).
bugs.fix: Record the former title in the image's `aka` list on rename, and add images_store.image_keys() returning canonical + former identities. apkg_image_sync matches against that set. Round-trip now reports 0 new images.

bugs.error_message: New records for yamxey/flura/mamoyen vanished after save_images(); the JSONL never contained them
bugs.root_cause: save_images dropped any record with no images via `if not all_images(rec) and is_illustratable(rec) and len(rec) <= 2`. A hypernym illustrated entirely by its hyponyms owns no image, so a derive-only record matched the drop condition and was silently discarded. The in-memory dict still looked right, which is why the first verification pass missed it -- it printed the mapping rather than reloading the file.
bugs.fix: Extracted is_empty_record(): a record survives if it has images, any sense with a `derive` spec, an illustratable=false marker, or any hand-added key on the record or a sense. Only a bare {word, senses} with plain empty senses is dropped. Verified by reloading from disk rather than trusting the in-memory mapping.

bugs.error_message: Adding a sense in the image curator was a placebo: the POST reported ok, the sense never persisted (reported on salamandra)
bugs.root_cause: is_empty_record dropped any record with no images. A word with no pictures that gains a freshly-created empty sense is exactly that, so save_images discarded it; the UI then re-read the store and honestly showed nothing. Same root cause as bug-186 (derive-only records) -- that was patched by special-casing `derive` instead of fixing the rule.
bugs.fix: is_empty_record now returns True only for a bare {word, senses:[]} with no hand-set keys. Any sense at all is intent, as is any unrecognised key on the record. Deleting the last sense still decays the record and cleans it up.

bugs.error_message: Editing a sense label in the image curator kicks you out of the field the moment you click into it
bugs.root_cause: The .sense container's click handler ran renderSenses(), which rebuilds the whole sense list. Clicking the label input bubbles up to that handler, so the input you just clicked into was destroyed and replaced mid-click.
bugs.fix: Selecting a sense no longer rebuilds the DOM: setActive(i) just toggles the .active class on the existing elements. The label input and PoS select also set the active sense on focus, and their change handlers return early when the value is unchanged, so tabbing through a field no longer triggers a save-and-rebuild.
